mission_08: Think of the cursor as a position: you want all rows that come AFTER the cursor in the sorted order. `ORDER BY order_date DESC, order_id DESC` means "newer dates first, and for same dates, higher IDs first."
The first condition `order_date < '2025-10-01'` captures all rows with an earlier date than the cursor — these definitely come after the cursor.
The second condition `order_date = '2025-10-01' AND order_id < 4500` handles same-date ties. For orders on the same date as the cursor, only those with a lower order_id come after it.
Combine both conditions with OR inside parentheses: `(order_date < '2025-10-01' OR (order_date = '2025-10-01' AND order_id < 4500))`. Keep the sort order as `ORDER BY order_date DESC, order_id DESC`.
